reference: Kabita Live current working-copy guide, restraint pass 2026-10-03 and portrait update 2026-10-04
scope: Book-relevant design and reader feature parity; preserve explicit Singhasan preferences

items.area: Shared palette, fonts, textures, icons and pagination source
items.decision: All 31 manifest items match their current Kabita Live sources; the upstream guide is refreshed. No wholesale visual-asset replacement is needed.
Keep the existing Contents and reader-tool search. User explicitly declined an additional search box on 4 October; this is a single 68-poem book.
Illustrated is the default reader with animation on; Quiet defaults to animation off. Separate saved choices, sound opt-in and reduced-motion override remain. Centre divider unchanged.

items.status: Applied and checked with private fixtures
items.decision: Language survives page turns, Exit reader and sharing. Unsupported translations explain the fallback to Odia. Private fixtures render with Source Serif 4, Noto Serif Tamil and Tiro Devanagari Hindi. Production language files remain empty.
Same illustrated front and back covers in both modes. Quiet hides only interior poem illustration leaves; text, page frame and reader tools are shared.
Three text sizes, language choices when ready, device-local marks/bookmarks, saved place, section chooser, paper surfaces, explicit turn/sound options and Exit reader.

Kabita Live Like row and collapsed Comments form; separate Singhasan Firebase service. Contact now submits directly to the private feedback collection with no email-draft step. Automatic email notification is not configured.

Named drawer, visible dismissal and focus return; light/dark/system preference. Mobile home and reader checked at 390px. Physical swipe, trackpad and assistive-technology review remain part of the user walkthrough.

items.area: Cover-story disclosure and restrained practical pages
items.decision: Kabita Live edition disclosures serve multi-issue browsing. Singhasan keeps the approved pictorial home narrative, dedicated covers and simple contact form. Do not replace those with a magazine template.

Final selection: masthead A, throne & earth beside Anek Odia title. Both A and B templates are retained; throne favicon unchanged. Compact earth footer with vertically aligned credit/navigation. Noto Serif Oriya remains the approved poem-reading font.
An old curd-bowl description now says milk pot, matching the user-confirmed source context. No poem text or illustration pixels changed.

items.area: Framework, catalogue search, analytics and accounts
items.decision: Keep the static build and dedicated Firebase service. Do not import magazine infrastructure, identities or analytics settings without a book-specific need.
No new generation, replacement, listening audition or alignment work. Existing published listening routes remain available.
Local linked checklist prepared. No user design approvals or human translation reviews inferred from automated checks.
